meta.title: Legal techniques: NAGA no-gi
meta.description: Which submissions and moves are legal under NAGA no-gi rules, by division.
meta.attribution: Data from bjj-data by Grapple Flows (https://grappleflows.com)
meta.disclaimer: Rules change. Check the official rulebook for your event before competing. Not affiliated with IBJJF, ADCC, NAGA, or Grappling Industries.

notes: Each row has one cell per column, in column order. "Y" legal, "N" illegal, "C" conditional: read the row note.
name: NAGA no-gi
penalty: See the NAGA rules for how illegal techniques are penalized at your event.

columns.label: Adult intermediate and expert (blue belt and up)

rows.label: Straight ankle lock
rows.note: Teens: no knee reaping on a straight ankle lock.

rows.label: Knee reaping
rows.note: NAGA sets no reaping restriction for adults. Teens may not reap on a straight ankle lock.

rows.label: Wrist lock
rows.note: Adult beginners must hold at least 3 fingers.

rows.label: Scissor takedown (kani basami)
rows.note: Legal for adults only if a hand is placed on the mat first.

rows.label: Slam
rows.note: Slamming on a takedown or to escape a position or submission is illegal for everyone.
